headline: YouTube testing hiding the dislike button on videos, moving it to a submenu
summary: Some users report the dislike button has been moved to the three-dots menu, making it significantly harder to access and potentially reducing its use.
details: YouTube is reportedly testing a change that moves the dislike button on videos into the three-dots submenu. Several users on X and Reddit have shared screenshots showing the button's new, less prominent location.

Currently, the dislike button sits directly next to the like button, making it easily accessible. Moving it to a submenu would require more effort to find and click, likely leading to fewer dislikes being registered.
The extent of this test is not yet clear, and Google has not provided an immediate comment on the reported changes. It's uncertain how widely this feature is being rolled out to users.

This isn't YouTube's first adjustment to the dislike feature. In 2021, the platform hid public dislike counts to protect creators from harassment, though creators can still view their own dislike data. Earlier this year, the dislike button was also removed from YouTube Shorts.
caption:
YouTube is reportedly testing a major change to its dislike button, moving it to a submenu. This could significantly impact how users interact with content.

YouTube is reportedly testing a change that moves the dislike button on videos into the three-dots submenu. Several users on X and Reddit have shared screenshots showing the button's new, less prominent location.

Currently, the dislike button sits directly next to the like button, making it easily accessible. Moving it to a submenu would require more effort to find and click, likely leading to fewer dislikes being registered.

The extent of this test is not yet clear, and Google has not provided an immediate comment on the reported changes. It's uncertain how widely this feature is being rolled out to users.

This isn't YouTube's first adjustment to the dislike feature. In 2021, the platform hid public dislike counts to protect creators from harassment, though creators can still view their own dislike data. Earlier this year, the dislike button was also removed from YouTube Shorts.
